title: Trainstorm Visual Asset
description: One entry in the visual asset registry: a reference to an image file plus governed metadata. Elements resolve this via render.asset_ref. The registry holds the reference and metadata only — never the image bytes. Owner: Brand + Localization (the same facet-owner as expression, per system-map.html).

asset_id.description: Stable identity, minted once, never reused or edited — the join key render.asset_ref points at. Human-legible slug (matches the atom_id/element_id convention), not positional. Do not rename even if content_hash later changes.

file.description: Path to the image file, relative to the registry. The ONLY embedded thing on this record is this reference — never the image bytes.

root.description: Which entry in the registry's `asset_roots` map this file resolves against. Absent means 'library' — the default bulk store. Deliberately a free string, not an enum: the roots are declared in the registry header, and duplicating that list here would be a second source of truth that drifts. A linter checks that every `root` names a declared root.

media_type.description: svg/png are render-pipeline-native (HTML/CSS -> headless render). Anything else should be converted on ingest, not at render time.

role.description: Governed, closed list — v0.1, draft. signature = rare/high-specificity brand asset, reserve for hero placements. motif = general-purpose illustrative asset tied to a recurring content concept, swappable within a family. chrome = decorative background/divider/texture, no semantic specificity, freely swappable. Unrecognized values are a schema violation, not a silent pass-through.

scope.description: Reuse breadth — orthogonal to role (a signature asset can be universal; a motif can be client-locked). Derived, not labeled: both empty = universal. industries non-empty, clients empty = usable by any client tagged with that industry. clients non-empty = restricted to exactly those clients, and wins over industries when both are set (narrowest scope binds). Not governed yet — industries/clients are free strings until a client/industry roster exists; typos won't be caught.

industries.description: e.g. ['pharma']. A client belonging to this industry may use the asset even if not individually listed in clients.

clients.description: e.g. ['astellas']. Non-empty means restricted to exactly these named clients, regardless of industry — the most restrictive setting.

mark_class.description: Governed, closed list — v0.1, draft. What KIND of mark this is, which `role: signature` alone cannot express. identity = the client's own corporate mark, governed by their brand team, outlives every engagement. sub_brand = a company or division they own (its own brand system; NOT interchangeable with the parent). program = an initiative/engagement mark, created for a project and retired with it. third_party = an external organisation's mark (regulatory agency, partner, standards body) — neither ours nor the client's, and carries its own usage restrictions. Required when role is 'signature'; meaningless otherwise. Absent is NOT the same as 'identity' — treat absent as unknown.
mark_class.$comment: Deliberately not named *_tier: the manifold already uses 'tier' for audience segments (tier1_field, tier2_msl) and the collision would mislead.

tags.description: Free-form descriptive tags for retrieval (subject, style, mood). Ungoverned — grows organically, unlike role.

content_type_hints.description: Optional: expression.content_type keys (from vocab/primitives.registry.json once populated) this asset pairs well with. Advisory and many-to-many — not a single-writer binding the way an atom's own expression facet is.

content_hash.description: Hash of the file's bytes. Flags when the underlying image actually changed (re-export, recolor, crop) versus when only metadata moved — same discipline as an atom's content_hash guarding its meaning.

usage_rights.description: e.g. 'original', 'licensed-stock', 'internal-generated'. Worth stating plainly before this becomes a shared library other agents pull from.

provenance.description: Where this came from, and how it was made or sourced.

then.$comment: A signature with no mark_class is exactly the ambiguity this field exists to remove — a program mark passing as the corporate identity.
